title: Updating Codes of Conduct and Whistle-blowing Framework for Political Office Holders and Public Officers
what_it_is: Updating Codes of Conduct and Whistle-blowing Framework for Political Office Holders and Public Officers

sections.label: Review of integrity rules
sections.summary: Questions are asked about reviewing rules on political office holders' interactions, gift declarations, and the Code of Conduct and whistle-blowing framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister in light of CPIB's findings on former Minister S Iswaran (a) whether the Minister-in-charge of the Public Service is currently undertaking a comprehensive review of the rules guiding the interactions of political office holders and officers of the public service with private sector stakeholders in social settings; and (b) whether any insight can be provided into the measures under consideration to enhance the guidelines to ensure utmost integrity in such engagements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister regarding the acceptance or obtainment of a valuable thing by public servants or political office holders (a) whether there is an established system for declarations of such gifts; (b) how is monitoring performed to detect absent or inadequate consideration of such declarations across the Government; and (c) whether governance and controls will be reviewed to further improve their effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister whether there are any plans to review or revise the Code of Conduct for Ministers and the whistle-blowing framework for public officers and to mandate refresher training on the Code of Conduct for public officers.

sections.label: Iswaran case facts needed
sections.summary: Knowing which rules apply to former Minister S Iswaran requires knowing his case facts, without prejudging them before trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To know which of these apply to the case of former Minister S Iswaran, we need to know the facts of his case, and we should not prejudge these facts before the court trial.

sections.label: Retaining gifts under $50
sections.summary: For operational simplicity, an officer may retain a gift worth less than $50 without paying, if Civil Service integrity is unaffected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For operational simplicity, the officer may be allowed to retain a gift worth less than $50 without paying for it, if doing so does not affect the integrity of the Civil Service.

sections.label: Code since 1954
sections.summary: The Code has been in place since 1954 and is regularly reviewed to remain sound and relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Code has been in place since 1954 and it is regularly reviewed to ensure that the Code remains sound and relevant.

sections.label: Internal Disclosure Policy reporting
sections.summary: Officers can report wrongful or doubtful practices to their Heads of Agencies, or beyond their organisation including to CPIB.

sentences.text: The Public Service has an established Internal Disclosure Policy where officers can directly report to their Heads of Agencies any wrongful or doubtful practices they observe.

If anyone suspects that any of their superiors have been compromised, they can report the suspicious activity to their Heads of Agencies, or beyond their organisation, including to agencies like CPIB.

sections.label: Reinforcing the Code
sections.summary: The Code is reinforced through on-boarding, annual declarations, mandatory quizzes, milestone programmes, senior leader discussions and service-wide reminders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Code is reinforced through various channels, including on-boarding of new entrants, annual declarations to remind officers of the rules, annual mandatory quizzes, incorporation into milestone programmes – for example, the Foundation Programme for Young Leaders, Management Development Courses for Supervisors, Senior Management Programme for Directors – and there will also be regular discussions and conversations with Senior Leaders on the values and ethos of our Public Service and there will also be regular service-wide reminders.
